channel.title: SpaceJumper
channel.description: Updates of SpaceJumper. .github/workflows/publish-release.yml adds an item for each published release.

item.description:
Added

  • Settings → macOS → Menu Bar: macOS's "Automatically hide and show the menu bar" (Always, On Desktop Only, In Full Screen Only, Never), and "Show the menu bar sooner" (off by default): the hidden menu bar slides in when the pointer reaches the top edge, after "Wait before showing" (0–300 ms; macOS waits 350 ms or longer), and hides 0.2 s after the pointer leaves it. An open menu keeps it shown.
  • Settings → macOS → Dock: switch macOS's "Automatically hide and show the Dock" on or off, sliders for how long the hidden Dock waits with the pointer at the edge of a desktop (macOS: 150 ms), how long the pointer has to push against the edge in a full-screen app (macOS: 250 ms; resting at the edge never shows the Dock there), and how long the Dock slides in and out (Off to macOS's default), and Restore Defaults. With both waits at Off, the Dock appears as soon as the pointer reaches the edge. The Dock restarts after a change to these settings. The README lists the keys of com.apple.dock they write.

Changed

  • Settings: a new macOS tab holds the Mission Control group ("Switch instantly with ⌘Tab" and the two macOS options), the Menu Bar group and the Dock group; General keeps the menu-bar number's settings (Menu Bar), Startup and Updates.
  • Settings: the macOS options "When switching to an application, switch to a Space with open windows for the application" and "Automatically rearrange Spaces based on most recent use" have a switch instead of Turn On / Turn Off; changing the rearranging restarts the Dock. The buttons that open System Settings are called System Settings… instead of Change….

Fixed

  • Changing macOS's "When switching to an application, switch to a Space with open windows for the application" from SpaceJumper (the Turn On / Turn Off button up to 0.6.0) stored the new value, but macOS kept switching as before until the Dock restarted. SpaceJumper now also passes the value to WindowServer, as System Settings does.

Changes since v0.6.0

  • b693ef3 Version bump to v0.7.0 (build 11)
  • afd3864 CHANGELOG: the macOS tab also holds the Menu Bar group
  • 6e629e8 Update the README screenshots, add the macOS tab
  • 2dabb41 Menu bar: hide 0.2 s after the pointer leaves, hidden setting for the delay
  • cc72222 Settings → macOS → Menu Bar: macOS's hiding choice and a sooner reveal
  • faa7a83 Settings: move Mission Control and Dock to a new macOS tab
  • 5a8fd54 Dock sliders: fixed descriptions, desktop wait up to 300 ms
  • 105ba72 Dock: sliders for both waits, and restart the Dock on slider release
  • 945b3fa Add Dock settings, switches for macOS options, and apply the ⌘Tab option
  • 296cd7e Release v0.6.0 (automatic appcast update)

Full diff: https://github.com/alberti42/SpaceJumper/compare/v0.6.0...v0.7.0

Added

  • Settings → General → Menu Bar → "Show the name of full-screen Spaces" (off by default): next to the number, the menu bar shows the name Mission Control shows for a full-screen Space, the app or both apps in split view. The first line of the menu names the app on a full-screen Space, whatever the setting.

Changed

  • Settings → Spaces: "Wrap around from the last Space to the first" is now in the Transition group, after Duration, with its explanation next to it.

Removed

  • The warning that another app had taken one of SpaceJumper's shortcuts (Settings → Spaces → Conflicts, the menu, Copy Diagnostics). macOS reports no error when two apps use the same keys, so the warning could not appear; Troubleshooting in the README explains what to do when an app shortcut does nothing.

Fixed

  • Settings, About, Copy Diagnostics, Check for Updates and Add App could open dimmed, as windows of an inactive app, until clicked: macOS declined SpaceJumper's activation while another app was active. SpaceJumper now takes over the activation from the frontmost app.

Changes since v0.5.0

  • 0eb1b08 Version bump to v0.6.0 (build 10)
  • dbd2c0e Update the README screenshots of the three Settings tabs
  • 1db3304 Remove the warning for shortcuts taken by another app
  • 3ef2798 Document that another app's global shortcut on the same keys goes unreported
  • 73ccb47 Take over activation from the frontmost app before showing a window
  • 15e38a9 Put wrap-around right after Duration in the Transition group
  • 8f02cec Move wrap-around into the Transition group
  • 44d9d0d Show the name of a full-screen Space next to its number
  • 39fbf0e Release v0.5.0 (automatic appcast update)
  • 8adc97a Lay out the README screenshots in tables, as in SyncGlass

Full diff: https://github.com/alberti42/SpaceJumper/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0

Added

  • An app icon: a desktop monitor whose screen shows a jump to hyperspace, in front of a night sky with stars. It follows macOS's light, dark, clear and tinted icon styles.
  • Settings → Spaces → Transition → "Cross-fade when Reduce motion is on" (on by default): turn it off to keep a short slide while Reduce motion stays on for the rest of macOS.
  • App shortcuts (Settings → Apps): give an app a letter, and the modifier keys chosen there (⌃⌘ by default) with that letter switch to the Space with the app's frontmost window, full-screen or not, and bring the app forward. An app that is not open is opened. The letter follows the keyboard layout (on a German keyboard ⌃⌘Z is the key labelled Z).

Changed

  • The menu-bar number and ⌃1 … ⌃9 count every Space by its position in Mission Control, full-screen apps included, so a full-screen app shows its number instead of "F". Settings → Spaces → Numbering → Desktops only keeps the previous numbering: only desktops, as macOS's "Switch to Desktop N" shortcuts count them.
  • Settings: the Shortcuts tab is now called Spaces, as the app shortcuts have their own tab, and the Transition group (Duration, Reduce motion) moved there from General.

Changes since v0.4.0

  • 6c14b23 Let typing a letter select it in an app's letter menu
  • ae72475 Version bump to v0.5.0 (build 9)

  • 5cbc0b9 Give app shortcuts their own modifier keys

  • c2e6512 Version bump to v0.4.1 (build 8)
  • b6359eb Show the app icon at the top of the README
  • 7e41618 Add the app icon
  • 4b940de Release v0.4.0 (automatic appcast update)

Full diff: https://github.com/alberti42/SpaceJumper/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0

Added

  • With Reduce motion on (System Settings → Accessibility → Motion) and a transition duration set, the Spaces cross-fade instead of sliding, as macOS does without SpaceJumper. Settings → General shows Reduce motion below the duration, with a Change… button.
  • Copy Diagnostics… in the menu: copies a plain-text report to the clipboard, for bug reports: versions, permissions, displays and Spaces, the settings of SpaceJumper and macOS, the shortcuts and their conflicts, the apps that intercept trackpad swipes or key presses, and SpaceJumper's recent activity. Nothing is sent over the Internet.
  • About SpaceJumper in the menu: macOS's About panel with the version, a short description, a link to the repository and the copyright line.

Changed

  • Settings → General: the slider "Slide animation" is now "Duration", in a group headed "Transition".

Changes since v0.3.1

  • 3b88b7b Version bump to v0.4.0 (build 7)
  • 5017a96 Add Copy Diagnostics to the menu
  • f5779a9 Cross-fade with WindowServer's screen transition
  • db8b492 Cross-fade between Spaces when Reduce motion is on
  • c5a1906 Name both options in the README's "⌘Tab no longer changes the Space"
  • 21442ef Simplify how the README explains ⌘Tab and hidden apps
  • 4270c9c Shorten the README and correct how ⌘Tab works
  • 6df5ede Shorten the Status section of the README
  • 3c64b88 State in the README that SpaceJumper works with SIP enabled
  • 482a32b Explain the slide on ⌘Tab to a hidden app in Troubleshooting
  • fa2ad28 Add an About window
  • 73723d0 Release v0.3.1 (automatic appcast update)

Full diff: https://github.com/alberti42/SpaceJumper/compare/v0.3.1...v0.4.0

Changed

  • ⌘Tab to a hidden app on another Space is left to macOS, which switches with its own slide. When the app is shown again, the Dock starts its switch by itself, even with the macOS option off, and sometimes before SpaceJumper learns of the activation; when SpaceJumper switched too, the two could mix.
  • With a slide length set, the new Space becomes current when the slide starts instead of when it ends; the menu bar changes at the start of the slide.
  • After a ⌘Tab switch, SpaceJumper makes the app active again only if macOS gives the focus to another app during the Space change (until 0.1 s after macOS announces it). A second ⌘Tab right after the first is no longer undone.

Fixed

  • With "Switch instantly with ⌘Tab" on, a switch by shortcut or swipe could bounce back to the previous Space. On every Space change macOS makes an app of the new Space active, sometimes one with no window there, such as Finder; SpaceJumper took that for an activation by the user and switched to that app's Space. Activations during a Space change are no longer followed.
  • With "Switch instantly with ⌘Tab" on, hiding or quitting the active app switched to the Space of the app macOS activated next. macOS stays on the current Space; so does SpaceJumper now.

Changes since v0.3.0

  • c65605b Version bump to v0.3.1 (build 6)
  • c4eab93 Remove a blank line inside the Unreleased Changed list
  • cd2f109 Leave ⌘Tab to a hidden app to macOS
  • 808d328 Do not follow activations after the active app hides or quits
  • 8d0e60b Stop following activations that come with a Space change
  • f86522f Release v0.3.0 (automatic appcast update)

Full diff: https://github.com/alberti42/SpaceJumper/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1

Added

  • Switch instantly with ⌘Tab (Settings → General → Mission Control, off by default): when ⌘Tab or the Dock activates an app with no window on the current Space, SpaceJumper switches to the Space of its frontmost window. It acts only while the macOS option "When switching to an application, switch to a Space with open windows for the application" is off. Settings shows that option next to the switch, with Turn Off (or Turn On, when both are off) and Change… buttons, and the menu points to Settings while the option still has to be turned off. A minimized window does not count, as in macOS. See "Switching with ⌘Tab" in the README.
  • Command-line mode: --app PID switches to the Space of that process's windows.

Changes since v0.2.0

  • d32dbef Version bump to v0.3.0 (build 5)
  • 20797c9 Offer to turn off macOS's switch for ⌘Tab, and document it
  • 1ef0953 Switch instantly when an app is activated
  • 9f52642 Say jump to lightspeed in the Star Wars sentence
  • 0008244 Name Star Wars in the v0.2.0 notes in the appcast
  • aebd54e Name Star Wars in the README's opening
  • de3c532 Describe the keyboard shortcuts in prose instead of a table
  • d9578f4 Add a security policy
  • 74852ec Show the Settings window in the README
  • a99984b Release v0.2.0 (automatic appcast update)
  • 1d3112d Separate related projects from the credits in the README

Full diff: https://github.com/alberti42/SpaceJumper/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0

InstantSpaces is now SpaceJumper, and it can slide too.

Ever wished you could jump between your Mac's Spaces like a Star Wars starship making the jump to lightspeed? SpaceJumper switches Spaces instantly, without macOS's slide. And if you'd like to see the jump, you can set how long it takes.

New name

InstantSpaces was too close to the name of InstantSpaceSwitcher, whose findings this app builds on. The app is now SpaceJumper, with a new bundle identifier, so macOS treats it as a new app:

  • InstantSpaces cannot update itself to SpaceJumper. It shows this release with a link to this page. Quit InstantSpaces, move it to the Trash, and install SpaceJumper below.
  • Your settings carry over: on first launch SpaceJumper copies the InstantSpaces settings (modifier keys, shortcut groups, swipes, wrap-around, updates).
  • Grant Accessibility again when macOS asks, and turn Open at Login on again if you used it.

Added

  • Slide animation (Settings → General, off by default): switches slide for the time you set, from 0 to 500 ms in 10 ms steps. SpaceJumper draws the slide itself, for the shortcuts and the swipes. ⌃1 … ⌃9 slide straight to the desktop, and wrap-around keeps the direction of the move.
  • The macOS settings that affect SpaceJumper are shown in Settings, each with a Change… button to its pane in System Settings:

- how swiping between Spaces is set in Trackpad → More Gestures (three fingers, four fingers or off); - whether macOS rearranges Spaces based on most recent use, which changes the desktop numbers.

  • A frame around the menu-bar number (Settings → General → Menu Bar), to tell it apart from other numbers in the menu bar: an outline, or a filled shape with the number cut out, as a rounded rectangle or a capsule (a circle around one digit).

Fixed

  • The Settings window comes to the front when opened from the menu; it could stay behind the active app.

Tested

Tested on one Mac with macOS 27.0.1, with Karabiner-Elements running. Still untested: macOS 26 and more than one display. Please report problems in the issues.

All changes since 0.1.1

Trackpad swipes inside Mission Control and App Exposé now behave as intended.

Changed

  • Mission Control: a swipe inside Mission Control switches to the next Space at once, as everywhere else. macOS's own swipe there can show a dark screen for about a second before the new Space appears; InstantSpaces avoids it. On macOS 27 this already happened in 0.1.0.

Fixed

  • App Exposé: a swipe inside App Exposé no longer switches Spaces. macOS doesn't switch there either, so InstantSpaces now leaves these swipes to macOS.

Tested

This release was tested on one Mac with macOS 27.0.1: keyboard shortcuts, trackpad swipes with natural scrolling on and off, swipes inside Mission Control and App Exposé, and full-screen Spaces. Still untested: macOS 26, several displays, and swipes with Karabiner-Elements running. Please report problems in the issues.

If you have 0.1.0, InstantSpaces offers this update by itself within a week, or at once when you choose Check for Updates in its menu.

All changes since 0.1.0

The first release of InstantSpaces, a menu-bar app that switches between Spaces without the slide animation. macOS has no setting to turn the animation off; "Reduce motion" only replaces it with a cross-fade. With InstantSpaces the new Space appears at once.

What it does

  • Keyboard shortcuts: ⌃← and ⌃→ move one Space left or right; ⌃1 … ⌃9 go to a desktop. All shortcuts share one set of modifier keys, which you choose in Settings: ⌃ (the default, as in macOS's own Mission Control shortcuts), ⌃⌥, ⌃⌘, ⌥⌘ or ⌃⌥⌘.
  • Trackpad swipes: swiping between Spaces with the trackpad switches at once too. This is on by default and can be switched off in Settings.
  • Wrap around (off by default): moving past the last Space, with the arrows or a swipe, goes to the first, and back.
  • Menu bar: shows the number of the current desktop, or "F" on a full-screen Space.
  • Settings window (⌘,): modifier keys, the shortcut groups, swipes, wrapping, Open at Login and updates. It lists the macOS shortcuts and other apps' shortcuts that use the same keys as yours.
  • Updates: InstantSpaces checks for a new version once a week, or when you choose Check for Updates in its menu.

Getting started

  1. Download InstantSpaces.zip below, unzip it and move InstantSpaces.app to the Applications folder.
  2. Open it. On first launch macOS asks whether InstantSpaces may use Accessibility. Allow it for instant trackpad swipes; the keyboard shortcuts work without it.
  3. With the default modifier ⌃, turn off macOS's own "Move left a space" and "Move right a space" in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Mission Control. Otherwise macOS switches as well, with its animation. InstantSpaces' Settings window lists any macOS shortcut that still uses the same keys.

Requirements and limits

  • macOS 26 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel. The app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
  • InstantSpaces uses private macOS interfaces, which Apple can change in any macOS update.
  • This release was tested on one Mac with macOS 27.0.1. Untested so far: macOS 26, several displays, full-screen Spaces, and trackpad swipes with natural scrolling off. Please report problems in the issues.
